item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00070","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C12","C02","C13"],"selected_candidate_label":"C12","confidence":0.76,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C12 plausibly supplied a material template for the child's treatment of executive-branch reorganization. Both letters invoke the Hoover Commission's recommendations, address congressional consideration or rejection of reorganization plans, defend modern principles of executive organization and management, and seek a path for implementing the Commission's remaining proposals. The child updates that machinery by asking the same Senate committee for modifications capable of securing acceptance of previously rejected plans. C02 provides related statutory and procedural background but is less closely aligned with the child's focus on Hoover Commission plans rejected by Congress. C13 shares the principle that detailed internal executive organization should remain administratively controlled, but its principal subject is federal aid to education.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"reorganization plans rejected by the last Congress ... revised plans might be presented to carry out the recommendations of the Hoover Commission","parent_excerpt":"If these plans fail, the whole great endeavor to reorganize the Executive Branch in accordance with modern principles of administration and management will be imperiled.","explanation":"Both frame congressional treatment of specific reorganization plans as the mechanism for carrying forward Hoover Commission recommendations."},{"child_excerpt":"suggestions ... on the modifications, consistent with the recommendations of the Hoover Commission, which are needed to obtain acceptance of these remaining plans","parent_excerpt":"There is nothing in Plan No. 1 which would preclude further reorganization, either by reorganization plan or by legislation.","explanation":"The child adapts C12's strategy of pursuing further Hoover-consistent reorganization through revised plans or legislation after congressional resistance."},{"child_excerpt":"carry out for that Department the basic recommendations of the Hoover Commission on departmental organization and management","parent_excerpt":"These plans are a first step in moving forward under reorganization authority on the wide range of proposals for greater efficiency and economy submitted by the Commission on Organization.","explanation":"Both characterize particular agency changes as installments in the broader implementation of the Commission's organization-and-management program."}]}
